'''''Iris planifolia''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the subgenus [[Iris subg. Scorpiris|''Scorpiris'']] of the genus ''[[Iris (plant)|Iris]]'', [[family (botany)|family]] Iridaceae. This [[bulbous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] from [[Southern Europe]] and [[North Africa]] has long, shiny green leaves, a short stem, and large scented flowers in various shades of blue.

==Description==
[[File:Elvas (49499002033).jpg|thumb|left|''Iris planifolia'' growing wild near [[Elvas]], Portugal]]
''Iris planifolia'' has a large brown ovoid bulb (around {{convert|2|in|abbr=on}} in diameter),<ref name=Lynch/> with fleshy cylindrical white roots.<ref name=american/><ref name=European/>

The shiny green leaves that grow up to {{convert|10|-|30|cm|abbr=on}} long and 1–3 cm wide<ref name=European/> can conceal the short stem<ref name=Lynch/> at flowering time. The leaves are [[lanceolate]], beginning narrow at soil level and growing up to a point.<ref name=american/> It is regarded as having one of the largest flowers in the subgenus ''Scorpiris''.<ref name=pacific/>

It can begin to flower in December,<ref name=ClaireAustin/> in January or February.<ref name=lathyrus/> In the wild it has been known to flower as late as Autumn.<ref name=alpine/> The flowers have a light scent,<ref name=ClaireAustin/> which can be described as spicy.<ref name=lathyrus/>

It is a short, stout plant with up to three large flowers per stem,<ref name=american/> which are generally 6–7 cm in diameter, with a perianth tube of 8–18 cm long. The falls are 5–8 cm long and the standards are 2 cm long.<ref name=European/> The plant can reach a maximum height of {{convert|10|-|15|cm|abbr=on}} tall.<ref name=alpine/>

The plant has flowers in various shades of blue,<ref name=lathyrus/> from bluish violet,<ref name=European/> bright sky blue,<ref name=rareplants/> and lilac blue,<ref name=ClaireAustin/> Like other irises, it has 2 pairs of petals, 3 large [[sepals]] (outer petals), known as the 'falls' and 3 inner, smaller petals (or [[tepals]]), known as the 'standards'.<ref name=ClaireAustin/> The falls have a dark blue veining and a yellow crest on the ridge.<ref name=European/><ref name=alpine/><ref name=rareplants/> It does not have a beard.<ref name=american/> Occasionally, white flowered forms can be found in the wild.<ref name=lathyrus/>

The plant has tiny football shaped [[pollen]] with small spikes.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tillie |first1=Nico |last2=Hall |first2=Tony |last3=İkinci |first3=Nursel |last4=Lliedo |first4=M |last5=Clarkson |first5=James |last6=Seisums |first6=Arnis |last7=Saito |first7=Takeshi |last8=Harley |first8=Madeline |last9=Chase |first9=Mark |title=Molecular phylogenetics of the juno irises, Iris subgenus Scorpiris (Iridaceae), based on six plastid markers |journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |date=17 October 2011 |volume=167 |pages=281–300 |doi=10.1111/j.1095-8339.2011.01176.x|doi-access=free }}</ref>

The capsule is oblong, sessile, like that of ''[[Colchicum]]'' on the surface of the soil in the centre of the leaves. It has brown seeds which can be as large as a pea.<ref name=american/>

==Taxonomy==
The [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] of 'planifolia' is derived from the [[Greek language|Greek]] word meaning 'with flat leaves'.<ref>{{cite book |last=Stearn |first=William |year=1972 |title=A Gardenerer's Dictionary of Plant Names |location=London |publisher=Cassell |page=257 |isbn=0304937215}}</ref>

It was first published by [[Théophile Alexis Durand|T.Durand]] and [[Hans Schinz|Schinz]] in 'Conspectus Floræ Africæ'  No.5. in 1894.<ref>{{cite web|title=Iris| page=143| url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=77111116-1|publisher=ipni.org (International Plant Names Index) |accessdate=17 September 2014}}</ref> But under the name ''Iris alata''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Plant Name Details |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/29402895#page/149/mode/1up |publisher=biodiversitylibrary.org| accessdate=17 September 2014}}</ref>

[[Adriano Fiori|Fiori]] and [[Giulio Paoletti|Paoletti]] in 'Flora Analytica d'Italia', recognized this species as the genus Iris from [[Philip Miller|Miller]]s original entry of ''Xiphium planifolium''. For many years this was known under the synonym. ''Iris alata'' by [[Jean Louis Marie Poiret|Poir]] and recorded in a 1939 checklist.<ref name=american>{{cite web|title=(SPEC) Iris planifolia (Miller) Fiori & Paoletti|date=20 April 2010 |url=http://wiki.irises.org/bin/view/Spec/SpecPlanifolia |publisher=wiki.irises.org (American Iris Society)|accessdate=17 September 2014}}</ref> Further research took then plant origin back to 1894.

''Iris planifolia'' is now the accepted name by the [[Royal Horticultural Society|RHS]],<ref name=rhs>{{cite web|title=Iris planifolia |url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/horticulturaldatabase/hortdatabase.asp?ID=101245 |publisher=www.rhs.org.uk| accessdate=17 September 2014}}</ref> and it was verified by [[United States Department of Agriculture]] and the [[Agricultural Research Service]] on 4 April 2003 and the updated on 3 December 2004.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref>
Note; ''Iris planifolia'' has over 20 different synonyms. See list in the infobox on the right. ''Iris alata'' (also commonly known as 'Scorpion Iris') is the most common synonym.<ref>Harry Thomas {{Google books|WNQIgZdepcgC|Round the Year in the Garden|page=243}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It is [[native plant|native]] to the [[Mediterranean Basin|Mediterranean regions]] of Europe and North Africa.<ref name=lathyrus/><ref name=grin/> This the only species in the Juno subgenus that can be found growing in Europe.<ref name=ClaireAustin/>

===Range===
It is found in [[Crete]], [[Greece]], [[Sicily]], [[Spain]], [[Portugal]],<ref name=ClaireAustin/> [[Sardinia]],<ref name=pacific/> (within North Africa) in [[Algeria]], [[Libya]], [[Tunisia]],<ref name=grin/> and [[Morocco]].<ref name=alpine/>

White forms of the iris can be found in [[Andalucia]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Topic: White Iris planifolia |date=7 January 2013 |url=http://andaluciabirdsociety.org/forum/index.php?topic=686.0 |publisher=andaluciabirdsociety.org |accessdate=17 September 2014 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304073043/http://andaluciabirdsociety.org/forum/index.php?topic=686.0 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Habitat===
''Iris planifolia'' is found on rocky hillsides,<ref name=pacific/> which are generally wet in the winter and dry in the summer.

==Cultivation==
[[File:Iris planifolia 02.JPG|thumb|left|''Iris planifolia'' at [[Bern Botanic Garden]]]]
It is [[Hardiness (plants)|hardy]] to [[USDA]] Zone 3.<ref name=European>James Cullen, Sabina G. Knees, H. Suzanne Cubey (Editors) {{Google books|CkxWrDqtWLQC|The European Garden Flora Flowering Plants: A Manual for the Identification|page=259}}</ref>

The bulb is a short lived plant. It is better grown in the UK, in a [[bulb frame]].<ref name=ClaireAustin>{{cite book | first= Claire | last=Austin | title= Irises: A Gardener's Encyclopedia | publisher= Timber Press, Incorporated | isbn = 978-0881927306 | year = 2005 | ol = OL8176432M | page=<!-- 287 in diff edition-->}}</ref> In pots or preferably in the ground.<ref name=pacific>{{cite web|title=Juno irises J-R| date=11 May 2014 |url=http://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/JunoIrisesTwo| publisher=www.pacificbulbsociety.org|accessdate=17 September 2014}}</ref>

It can also be cultivated in pots.<ref name=Lynch>Richard Lynch {{Google books|grvYTul5CSUC|The Book of the Iris|page=185-186}}</ref> But the pots need to be a minimum of 30 cm tall (or 1 ft), to allow maximum root space.<ref name=pacific/>

It needs good ventilation to prevent disease,<ref name=american/> but can be prone to virus infections.<ref name=lathyrus>{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Rowland|title=Iris planifolia|year=2010|url=http://www.lathyrus-seed.com/paradise/flowers/planifolia.html|publisher=lathyrus-seed.com|accessdate=17 September 2014|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304001553/http://www.lathyrus-seed.com/paradise/flowers/planifolia.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Causing a loss of growth, and causes pale or streaky foliage. Infected plants should be destroyed to stop contamination of other plants.<ref name=alpine>{{cite web|title=Iris planifolia |year=2011 | url=http://encyclopaedia.alpinegardensociety.net/plants/Iris/planifolia| publisher=encyclopaedia.alpinegardensociety.net |accessdate=17 September 2014}}</ref>

For good growth next year, it prefers a good warm dry ripening period in summer,<ref name=lathyrus/> in sharply drained soil.<ref name=rareplants>{{cite web|title=Iris planifolia|url=http://rareplants.co.uk/product.asp?strParents=192&CAT_ID=108&P_ID=1900|publisher=rareplants.co.uk|accessdate=17 September 2014|archive-date=5 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220605041022/http://www.rareplants.co.uk/product.asp?strParents=192&CAT_ID=108&P_ID=1900|url-status=dead}}</ref>

It can be propagated naturally as it creates clumps of bulbs, that can be divided, by being very carefully teased apart in late summer. Care mus be taken not to damage the fleshy roots.<ref name=lathyrus/>
